identity.title: [v0.92.1][Sidecar] Harden and retain the AWS GPU Shepherd proof runner

values.summary: Two real Terraform launches have now proved the GPU half and cleanup. The latest run passed immutable bootstrap, two-model VRAM residency, Git-free source restoration, and reached Runtime validation, where it exposed a Vector install-root mismatch and failed with exit 69. Both nodes and volumes were destroyed. The install and validator paths now share one explicit root; final paid proof remains pending review and rerun.
actual_changes: Retained the reviewed Terraform-owned two-node topology, one key pair, mandatory SSH /32, private Ollama routing, immutable artifacts, single-use authorization, cost bound, and three cleanup paths.
Replaced the hung single PUT with multipart upload plus fail-closed immutable VersionId verification.
Observed two real GPU receipts proving llama3.1:8b and qwen3:8b simultaneously resident with exact digests and nonzero VRAM while Ollama remained non-public.
Made HOME=/root explicit in both bootstrap scripts and the Ollama systemd unit after the first Runtime failure.
Reduced the exact reviewed source archive from 335 MiB to 25 MiB with complete local Rust path-dependency closure and Git-free authorization-bound revision validation.
Observed the second Runtime node fail with exit 69 because the verified Vector installer used the repository default root while the validator was pointed at /opt/adl-issue345/vector.
Set ADL_VECTOR_INSTALL_ROOT and ADL_RUNTIME_VECTOR_BIN from the same explicit vector_root and fail closed unless that exact binary is executable.
Extended the generated-bootstrap contract test to prove installer, validator, and executable checks use the same Vector root.
Confirmed controller cleanup drove both instances to termination, removed all run volumes, destroyed Terraform state resources, and released the lock after both failed attempts.

actual_validation.purpose: Prove twenty-four no-paid topology, bootstrap, Vector-root, Git-free archive, IAM, authorization, recovery, and cleanup contracts.
Run the real Terraform two-node qualification through GPU residency, Runtime validation, failure receipt, and cleanup.
Validate the complete two-node Terraform configuration.
